#+title: Native workspace recipe contract

* Supported interface
Native workspace production uses the closed version2 request below on
x86_64-linux. Ordinary Source discovery, application production and the Rust
pre-BEAM consumer use the same fixed Nix recipe and independent product
verification. The workspace must be self-contained and produce a cdylib.

The [[../../research/authoritative-nix-production/STATUS.org][qualification record]] distinguishes passing component controls from final
SDK and exact-current-consumer acceptance. Workspace support does not close
language/runtime execution obligations or authorize a different native host.

* Request and provenance
#+begin_src json
{"version":2,"source":"/nix/store/WORKSPACE-SNAPSHOT",
 "member":"crates/engine","package":"rust-engine","crate":"engine",
 "abi":"beam-lisp-native-engine-v1","target":"x86_64-linux"}
#+end_src

source names the complete explicit workspace closure root. It contains the
root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, selected member, sibling path dependencies and
supporting files. member is the package directory relative to that root;
"." selects a root package. package must equal that manifest's package.name.
crate remains the BL-facing library identity. Cargo's lib.name can differ.
Rustler's init! host must still match the namespace containing defnative;
changing the publication alias does not rename or authorize that BEAM host.

The version2 artifact retains exact source/member/package/crate/abi/target,
records cargoLibrary as the actual Cargo library name, and publishes the stable
lib/<crate>.so path. Toolchain identity, final-byte digest, compiled product and
worker observations remain in the manifest. Version1 request and artifact
fields remain compatible with standalone crates.

* Snapshot and validation
native-source.nix and native-snapshot.nix accept version (default1), member
(default".") and package (default null). Version2 requires package explicitly.
The snapshot omits .git, .bl and target directories and refuses symlinks or
special files. Direct version2 store inputs must already be filtered snapshots.

Validation parses the root, selected member and transitive path dependencies.
It checks ordinary/dev/build/target-specific/workspace dependency tables and
patch/replace declarations. Paths normalize within the captured root; absolute
or escaping paths and reserved build/cache paths refuse. Cargo owns workspace
member-glob expansion and complete locked-workspace consistency. Unused invalid
Cargo.toml test fixtures are retained as support bytes without being parsed.

Workspace-inherited package versions are resolved from workspace.package.
Member paths are bounded ASCII relative segments: no empty/dot/dot-dot,
reserved or leading-hyphen segments; each segment is at most255 characters,
and the whole member is at most4096 characters. Cargo package names and Rust
library/BL crate identifiers are bounded to128 characters. Path normalization
is bounded to4096 characters, source depth to64, and the inspected manifest
closure to1024 entries.

* Build behavior
The fixed recipe passes --lib, --manifest-path <member>/Cargo.toml and --package
<package>. It pins CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target so project Cargo configuration cannot
redirect publication. Cargo.lock is always the root lock. All compilation
remains in the bounded KVM worker; no writable Cargo target is published.

Version2 snapshots have a workspace-wide name, and compiled products use the
Cargo package/library identity. Changing only the BL alias or ABI label changes
the wrapper without changing the Rust compile inputs. The existing desktop
profile follows the selected Cargo/library identity for version2. Additional
system-dependency profiles remain separate declared-recipe work.

* Main-thread qualification cases
- Existing version1 standalone realization and BL/Rust byte agreement.
- Workspace root with inherited version, a differently named cdylib, and a
  sibling path dependency; invoke the resulting native function.
- Root package plus nested path dependency; transitive ../sibling paths that
  normalize inside the root; workspace.dependencies and target/build/dev paths.
- Root Cargo.lock and support-file/build.rs changes affect the product;
  generated target noise does not affect a normal snapshot.
- Alias-only and ABI-only changes reuse compiled while final manifests differ.
- An unused deliberately invalid Cargo.toml fixture does not block the package.
- Absolute/escaping/missing dependency paths, symlinks, invalid member/package,
  wrong package/member pairing, missing root lock and malformed requests refuse.
- Cyclic path closure terminates validation; Cargo still owns semantic rejection.
- Non-default target-dir configuration still publishes from the pinned tree.

* Rust consumer interface and verifier scope
The pre-BEAM consumer preserves prepare(tree, source, name, custody) as the
version1 wrapper. prepare_request(tree, request, custody) accepts the same
closed version1/version2 object as the fixed recipe. It validates the request
before launching processes, installs and verifies the source-retention root,
then realizes the native product remotely and verifies its final retention.
Version2 snapshot arguments include explicit version/member/package.

Verification independently compares version/source/crate/ABI/target and,
for version2, exact member/package. cargoLibrary must be a bounded Rust
identifier, compiled must name a top-level store object, and the regular
compiled/lib/<cargoLibrary>.so must have the same SHA256 as the regular final
lib/<crate>.so. The fixed Nix recipe parses Cargo.toml and owns actual Cargo
package/library selection. The Rust verifier intentionally adds no partial TOML
parser or verification subprocess; its checks establish identity/byte
consistency, not language execution authority or independent compile causality.

Additional main-thread Rust cases:
- Closed version1 and version2 requests accept; missing/unknown fields, invalid
  versions, malformed/bounded member/package/crate/ABI/source fields refuse.
- A real Source-produced version2 receipt passes Rust verification and
  prepare_request selects the same product bytes with a retained source root.
- A changed member/package/version refuses even when library bytes are intact.
- Changed cargoLibrary naming a missing/different compiled library refuses.
- A non-store compiled address, compiled symlink, or cross-object compiled
  pointer with different library bytes refuses before publication.
- Existing standalone prepare and Source/Rust cross-consumer controls remain.
- Native workspace validator edits change stamp_inputs and invalidate reuse.

* Project declarations and everyday use
Declare workspace selection in env.bl. The source is the entire closure root,
not the selected member directory. Keep the workspace Cargo.lock there.
#+begin_src clojure
{:build
 {:native ["native/*"
           {:source "rust/workspace"
            :member "crates/engine"
            :package "rust-engine"
            :crate "engine"
            :abi "beam-lisp-native-engine-v1"}]}}
#+end_src
The string entry preserves existing standalone discovery. The map selects a
Cargo package explicitly while publishing priv/native/engine.so, even when
Cargo's lib.name differs. Duplicate publication aliases refuse. Remove the
string when all native products live in explicitly declared workspaces.

Normal project native builds and vm.native/build! select the same declared
alias through the authoritative Nix producer; neither needs a backend flag or
per-command remote-builder option. Existing output custody and atomic library
selection apply to both request versions. Remote execution is selected by the
host/artifact configuration, independently of these source declarations.

The pure bl.native-declarations/normalize entry returns [declarations errors]
for env validation. discover! expands paths to canonical request option maps,
with absolute source, version, crate, abi and target; workspace maps additionally
carry member and package. It reads directory entries and Cargo.toml existence,
never evaluates project or Cargo code. Missing/empty declarations retain the
native/* convention. Explicit workspace source validation remains the fixed
snapshot recipe's responsibility.

build/build-native supports [root log] for ordinary project discovery and
[root log declarations] for sealed workers. build/produce! accepts
:native-declarations to forward captured declarations without rediscovering a
mutable project. Application source capture includes each complete declared
workspace root and projects canonical nativeProducts source paths relative to
the application root. The fixed application recipe prepares those products;
the worker reads the captured env.bl through normal discovery and consumes its
verified prepared-native set. It does not forward expanded producer maps as
:native-declarations: that option accepts original declaration maps/strings.

Main-thread declaration checks should cover legacy globs; workspace aliases
that differ from package/lib names; two selected members sharing one root;
normalization against an explicit root rather than cwd; unknown/missing fields;
member traversal/empty segments and bounded identifiers; duplicate aliases;
single-alias vm.native/build! selection; and sealed application requests using
the same expanded products as an ordinary native build.

* Automatic refresh and closure changes
Automatic native refresh reads each source-backed project's normalized env.bl
independently. Consumer declarations select consumer products; the engine tree
retains its own declarations and publication root. A declared workspace does
not need a native/ directory to participate. Output paths use the declared
crate alias, while refresh identities include source/member/package/crate/ABI.

Refresh hashes the complete captured workspace closure, including root lock,
sibling dependencies, build scripts, Cargo configuration and arbitrary support
files. Adding/removing support files or changing executable bits invalidates
the receipt. .git, .bl and target subtrees are ignored. Multiple aliases sharing
a root reuse one source inventory. Existing output custody, artifact byte
verification and native host admission remain in place; a refresh receipt does
not grant permission to execute a different host.

Inventories reject filesystem root, symlink source ancestors, internal symlinks
and special files. Traversal is deterministic and limited to 65,536 entries,
64 levels, 128 MiB per file and 1 GiB of source bytes per closure. Exceeding a
bound refuses refresh explicitly. Legacy glob expansion retains existing
language discovery behavior; expansion itself is not separately bounded by
this inventory, which applies to each selected closure after discovery.

Main-thread checks should modify sibling Rust dependencies, Cargo.lock,
non-Rust build-script support files and executable modes; verify a second
unchanged refresh uses the receipt; verify generated target noise does not
invalidate it; and check consumer/platform aliases remain isolated. Add
symlink-ancestor/internal-link/root-scan and capacity refusal cases. Actual
native alias loading must still pass the existing native host admission path.

* Runnable workspace showcase
examples/artifacts/workspace/ contains a self-contained project with a nested
Rust workspace. Its env.bl declares source="rust", member="crates/engine",
package="artifact-workspace-engine", crate="workspace_demo" and
abi="beam-lisp-native-workspace-demo-v1". The actual Cargo library is
workspace_engine_nif. The sibling artifact-workspace-support package reads
support/answer.txt and support/message.txt using include_str!, so the example
exercises captured bytes outside the selected crate and its Rust src tree.

From examples/artifacts/workspace/, run ../../../bin/bl --cold run showcase.bl.
Normal build discovery selects the declared member, publishes
priv/native/workspace_demo.so, and the artifact.workspace namespace calls its
ordinary (defnative "workspace_demo" (answer 0) (support-message 0)) functions.
Initial JSON contains answer42 and supportMessage="workspace support is
captured". Set rust/support/answer.txt to43 and invoke with BL_WORKSPACE_EXPECTED=43
to check that a new immutable product returns changed support bytes. Restore
the file afterward. Start a fresh process for each NIF loading check.

The example README records the identities and exact commands. Its lockfile
retains the existing native/bl_json Rustler closure and checksums, with new
workspace package records. The recorded component controls exercise locked
station compilation, the actual BL NIF call and a support mutation returning43
through a private Source receiver. Those observations do not qualify a later
SDK automatically: the exact-current-SDK walkthrough remains a separate gate.
See [[../../research/authoritative-nix-production/STATUS.org][qualification record]] and the workspace-showcase logs it identifies.
